judgment.rationale: Treat this as a keyboard-layout compatibility defect, not merely a missing VK_RMENU check after WM_HOTKEY. Registration can consume the chord before that handler runs. A coordinated registration/configuration policy must preserve the intended capture/mirror variants while avoiding character-entry collisions. If unfixed, ordinary text entry loses characters whenever the colliding feature is active.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the exact derived registered chords on affected layouts and design an explicit layout-safe variant policy; do not silently remove shortcut variants or claim contributor test results as local validation.
evidence: The complete discussion reports German/Danish AltGr+9 interference and a latest Portuguese report on0.102.3001; disabling or changing the feature shortcut restores the character.
A contributor supplies tests/recordings and explains derived record/mirror modifier combinations; these results are attributed, not independently executed.
Immutable current-main Zoomit.cpp derives mirror crop/window and recording window variants using XOR with Shift/Alt and registers them with RegisterHotKey.

title: Default Mirror Activation shortcut conflicts with non-US keyboard layouts

prerequisites: Windows test account with German, Danish and Portuguese keyboard layouts.
Record base/derived shortcut settings and use a plain text editor for character entry.
steps: For each reported layout, type the reported AltGr character with ZoomIt disabled and enabled using the reported/default shortcut settings.
List the actual registered base/crop/window chords and repeat after remapping only the conflicting base shortcut.
Compare registration-time delivery and WM_HOTKEY handling; test both record and mirror variants and layout changes.
reproduce.expected: Normal AltGr character entry is preserved while supported capture/mirror variants remain usable through documented/configured chords.

fix_assessment.rationale: The current registration mechanism and repeated workaround reports support a specific fix direction; exact layout/chord coverage and the desired configurable policy still require validation.

proposed_fixes.title: Prevent derived ZoomIt shortcuts from consuming AltGr text entry
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Derived global Ctrl+Alt registrations can overlap AltGr character chords. Checking right-Alt only after a registered hotkey is delivered cannot return the consumed character to its target application.
verification: Affected AltGr characters type normally with ZoomIt active and each supported base/derived configuration.
Record/mirror full-screen, crop and window shortcuts remain accessible and match their documented/UI chords.
Test settings changes, input-layout changes, registration conflicts and ordinary non-AltGr shortcuts; verify behavior before and after registration, not only WM_HOTKEY handling.

confidence.rationale: Current code and several reported disable/remap comparisons support the collision mechanism; the final compatibility policy and independent layout matrix have not been validated.

plan: Enumerate base and derived record/mirror chords from actual settings and reproduce reported character loss on German, Danish and Portuguese layouts.

Choose an explicit collision-aware or user-configurable variant registration policy that preserves access to crop/window modes; handle registration failure visibly instead of swallowing text or silently dropping a feature.
Apply the policy consistently to record and mirror registration, shortcut display and settings updates, with tests for derived chords and layout changes.
